Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Remove the legacy two-way choice code from storylines

## Problem statement

The core story-line system still carries the original **two-way choice** data
model (`hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`) as a transitional
fallback alongside the generalised `options` model, plus the two-way
`ChoiceClarityLabels` presentation API (`StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels`
/ `defaultChoiceClarityLabels`). Two compilation paths, two authoring/editor
field sets, two validation vocabularies and a two-button label API must be
maintained, and editors can silently no-op when they edit the legacy links of
an `options`-authored card. The generalised model (`options` encoding +
programmatic registry) now covers every shipped case, so the legacy model and
its clarity-label API should be deleted end-to-end.

The work item seed explicitly waives backward compatibility and directs that
the `../tce-main-street` story-lines be inspected; if they use the legacy
structure, a **critical** work item must be created in that project to update
them. The producer has additionally confirmed that `ChoiceClarityLabels` is
in scope for retirement.

## Users

- **Engine maintainer** — "As the maintainer of `src/story-line/`, I want one
  option model and one compilation path so I no longer carry dead transitional
  code and conditional `hasChoices` branches."
- **Game developer (Main Street / future games)** — "As a game developer, I
  want a single documented way to author choices (`options` encoding or the
  registry) so my content, adapter, CLI and editor all agree."
- **Content designer** — "As a content designer, I want the editor and
  `storylines:author` CLI to expose only supported fields, so an edit cannot
  silently do nothing because it wrote a legacy link column."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runtime model and clarity-label API removed.** `StorylineCard.hasChoices`,
   `acceptNextCardId` and `rejectNextCardId` are gone from `src/story-line/types.ts`;
   `compileStorylineFromEvent` compiles only from registered options or a
   non-empty CSV `options` encoding (no Accept/Reject fallback), and
   `eventHasStoryline` no longer consults `hasChoices`. `ChoiceClarityLabels`,
   `StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels` and `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` are
   removed from the public API (and their `index.ts` exports). A bare
   `storylineId` still does **not** make a card a choice. All shipped content
   compiles to exactly the same option lists as before.
2. **Content/authoring/editor toolchain removed.** The content model
   (`ContentCard`, `ContentFieldMapping`, `mappedFieldColumns`), CSV
   projection (`cardsFromCsv`), content compilation (`compileContentOptions`,
   `contentCardHasChoice`), validator (`orphan-link` / `dangling-link` legacy
   rules), `mutate` specs, editor view-model/field-descriptors/`linkKind`
   edits, `storyline-author` CLI flags, and the visual editor forms no longer
   model, read, write, validate or expose the three legacy fields. A derived
   *choice-node* flag (e.g. the manifest's `hasChoices`) may remain **only** if
   it is computed purely from compiled options.
3. **Content artefacts, fixtures and schema aligned.** The Gym demo content
   (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`) drops the three legacy columns
   and `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER` stops mapping them; the committed Gym manifest /
   Mermaid artefacts regenerate with no drift (`npm run storylines:graph --
   --check`); card-pack fixtures, reference CSVs and
   `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` are updated consistently.
4. **Main Street investigated and follow-up filed.** `../tce-main-street` is
   inspected. Because its CSV header, `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_ADAPTER`,
   `EventCard` type, transcript schema, `MainStreetStorylineJournal`
   (`ChoiceClarityLabels` re-export + `choiceClarityLabels`) and storyline
   helpers still declare the legacy columns/fields/API, a **critical** work
   item is created in the `tce-main-street` Worklog to remove them and migrate
   its loader/resolution/presentation to the `options`-only model (push to
   `dev` only).
5. **Docs and tests.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`,
   `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` and `docs/dev/card-packs-runbook.md`, and no
   reference to the three legacy fields remains in `src/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`,
   `schemas/` or `example-games/`. Unit and browser tests are updated (legacy
   fixtures replaced with `options` equivalents), the changed-scope test gate
   passes, and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Backward compatibility is explicitly **not** required (seed).
- Preserve every generalised-model behaviour: arbitrary labels, ordered
  candidate successor sets, terminal options, `effectPolicy: 'apply'` for CSV
  options, registry precedence, conditional/cost draw-time filtering, and
  exactly one seeded `rng()` draw per random successor selection.
- `StorylineOption.successorId` is **not** part of the legacy two-way removal:
  it remains the registry seam field and the lowest-precedence single successor.
- `ChoiceClarityLabels` **is** retired (producer instruction). The
  `accept`/`reject` narrative wording in `defaultStoryUpdateLine` remains: it is
  driven by the option label, not by the retired label API, and Main Street's
  dialogs still present Accept/Reject option labels.
- Core must stay Phaser-free and game-free; the content toolchain must load
  under `tsx` and keep byte-identical CSV round-trips.
- Multi-repo: core changes land in this repo; Main Street changes are tracked
  in its own Worklog store and pushed to `dev` only (never `main`).
- No `wl list` without a search term; use the standard `build → test → commit`
  order during implementation.

## Existing state

- The generalised option model was introduced by MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5 and
  generalised into core by CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S; the legacy fields were kept
  transitionally.
- Main Street `src/card-data.csv`: **no** row populates the three legacy
  columns (all blank / `false`); 7 rows use the `options` encoding.
- Gym `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`: the three legacy columns are
  present in the header but every row has them blank / `false`; 3 rows use
  `options`.
- The committed Gym manifest and schema still carry a (derived) `hasChoices`
  node flag.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` still documents the legacy compilation
  precedence, the "game without a legacy two-way choice model" adapter
  guidance, and the `choiceClarityLabels` UI-adapter method.
- `StorylineUiAdapter` still requires `choiceClarityLabels`, implemented by
  `defaultChoiceClarityLabels`; Main Street re-exports the type and wraps the
  method in `MainStreetStorylineJournal`.

## Desired change

Delete the legacy two-way choice model and the `ChoiceClarityLabels` API
end-to-end, leaving a single `options`/registry-driven choice model, and align
content, editor, CLI, schema, fixtures, docs and tests. Coordinate the coupled
Main Street clean-up through a new critical item in that repo.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/story-line/types.ts` — remove `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`,
  `rejectNextCardId` from `StorylineCard` and remove the `ChoiceClarityLabels`
  interface + the `choiceClarityLabels` method from `StorylineUiAdapter`.
- `src/story-line/ui-adapter.ts` — remove `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` and the
  `choiceClarityLabels` entry in `createDefaultStorylineUiAdapter`.
- `src/story-line/index.ts` — drop the `ChoiceClarityLabels` type export and the
  `defaultChoiceClarityLabels` helper export.
- `src/story-line/compile.ts` — delete the legacy Accept/Reject compilation
  branch and the `hasChoices` clause in `eventHasStoryline`.
- `src/story-line/content/types.ts` — drop legacy fields from `ContentCard` /
  `ContentFieldMapping` / `mappedFieldColumns`; reword adapter docs.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — stop projecting/compiling the legacy
  columns; `contentCardHasChoice` becomes options-only.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — remove the `orphan-link` /
  `dangling-link` legacy-link rules and their docs.
- `src/story-line/content/mutate.ts` — drop legacy fields from add/update specs.
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — derive choice-ness from compiled
  options only (keep or rename the derived node flag).
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — drop legacy columns/mappings/defaults
  from `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER`.
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — drop `hasChoices` from the node model
  (keep a derived choice flag if the viewer needs it).
- `src/story-line/editor/field-descriptors.ts` — delete the legacy field
  descriptors and parsing/formatting cases.
- `src/story-line/editor/edits.ts` — remove `linkKind`/legacy link-update path.
- `tools/storyline-editor/add-card-form.ts` — remove the legacy-link capability
  check.
- `tools/storyline-editor/graph-renderer.ts` / `app-shell.ts` — use the derived
  choice flag, not the legacy field.
- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — remove `--has-choices`, `--accept-next`,
  `--clear-accept-next`, `--reject-next`, `--clear-reject-next` flags.
- `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` — keep the derived flag or rename
  it consistently.
- `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`,
  `example-games/gym/content/storyline-manifest.json`,
  `example-games/gym/content/storyline-graph.mmd` — drop legacy columns and
  regenerate artefacts.
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/*.csv`,
  `tests/fixtures/card-pack/**/cards.csv`,
  `tests/fixtures/reference-packs/**/cards.csv`,
  `tests/story-line/content/fixture-adapter.ts` — migrate fixtures to `options`.
- `tests/story-line/compile.test.ts`, `resolve.test.ts`, `ui-adapter.test.ts`,
  `content/{adapters,csv,validate,manifest,author}.test.ts`,
  `editor/{view-model,edit-forms,bridge,preview-validate,edit-roundtrip,viewer}.test.ts`
  — update/remove legacy assertions and keep coverage of the generalised model.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md`,
  `docs/dev/card-packs-runbook.md` — reword to the single option model.
- `../tce-main-street/src/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts`,
  `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`, `MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
  `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` (drop the `ChoiceClarityLabels` re-export and
  `choiceClarityLabels` wrapper), `src/card-data.csv` — coupled clean-up
  tracked by the new critical Main Street item; its
  `tests/main-street/storyline-journal.test.ts` and
  `storyline-behaviour-parity.test.ts` cover the retired labels.

## Related work

- CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S — Storyline content and authoring toolchain generalised
  into core (introduced the `options` model; legacy retained transitionally).
- CG-0MVHZ2N2X0082OW7 — Editor host and read-only graph viewer.
- CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD — Storyline management UI.
- CG-0MVHY82PQ004Q3B9 — Manually test the story-line extraction (Gym demo +
  Main Street storylines).
- CG-0MVKNC9MY006ULES — Gym storyline demo: extract pure logic and unit-test it.
- MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5 — CSV option encoding and compilation (Main Street;
  introduced `options`, intended to retire the three legacy columns).
- MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI — Extract the storyline features (Main Street).
- MS-0MUZKA9CJ000N144 — Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision — `ChoiceClarityLabels` retired.** The producer confirmed the
  accept/reject clarity-label API is in scope; it is removed from `types.ts`,
  `ui-adapter.ts` and `index.ts`. The `accept`/`reject` narrative wording in
  `defaultStoryUpdateLine` is retained (label-driven, separate from the retired
  API) unless the producer asks for that too.
- **Assumption — `successorId` retained.** It is the registry seam and the
  lowest-precedence single successor, not part of the two-way removal.
- **Assumption — derived choice flag retained.** The manifest's node choice
  flag (currently `hasChoices`) may stay if computed purely from compiled
  options; renaming is optional polish, not required.
- **Risk — silent behaviour drift.** Removing the fallback could change
  compilation for a content row that relied on `hasChoices` with no `options`.
  Mitigation: grep all fixtures/content first; no shipped row populates the
  legacy columns (verified), so expected drift is zero for shipped content.
- **Risk — cross-repo breakage.** Main Street compiles against the core
  submodule; deleting the exported fields and the `ChoiceClarityLabels` API
  breaks its build until its own item lands. Mitigation: file the critical Main
  Street item as part of this work and land/pin the submodule bump together.
- **Risk — schema/artefact drift.** `--check` guards must stay green; regenerate
  committed Gym artefacts in the same commit.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Renaming the derived manifest node flag is recorded
  as optional polish, not folded into this item unless the producer says
  otherwise. Retiring the `defaultStoryUpdateLine` accept/reject narrative
  wording is likewise a separate decision if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does the removal include the `ChoiceClarityLabels` accept/reject UI
  labels and the `accept`/`reject` narrative wording, or only the legacy
  `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` data model?" — Answer
  (producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-02): "Also retire the
  ChoiceClarityLabels". The brief therefore retires `ChoiceClarityLabels`,
  `StorylineUiAdapter.choiceClarityLabels` and `defaultChoiceClarityLabels`.
  The `accept`/`reject` narrative wording in `defaultStoryUpdateLine` is
  retained (label-driven, separate API) unless the producer says otherwise.
  Source: producer reply in this session; repo research
  (`src/story-line/types.ts`, `ui-adapter.ts`,
  `../tce-main-street/src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`).
- Q: "Do the Main Street story-lines use the legacy structure?" — Answer
  (repo research): **No data row does**; all three legacy columns are blank /
  `false` in `src/card-data.csv`, and 7 rows use the `options` encoding.
  However the combined CSV *header*, `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_ADAPTER`, `EventCard`
  type, transcript schema and storyline helpers still declare the legacy
  columns/fields, and `MainStreetStorylineJournal` still re-exports
  `ChoiceClarityLabels` and wraps `choiceClarityLabels`. Therefore, once core
  removes them, a **critical** Main Street work item is required. Source:
  `../tce-main-street/src/card-data.csv`,
  `MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts`, `MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`,
  `MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
  `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`.
- Q: "Is backward compatibility required?" — Answer (seed): **No**.
  Source: work item description.
- Q: "Is there an existing completed item that already removes this?" — Answer
  (Worklog search): **No**; MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5 introduced `options` and
  CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S generalised the toolkit, but neither removed the legacy
  fields. Source: `wl search` for "legacy", "two-way choice",
  "hasChoices"; `wl show CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV** – Citadel variant option for Beleaguered Castle (completed)
- **CG-0MVHZ2N2X0082OW7** – Editor host and read-only graph viewer (completed)
- **CG-0MVHY82PQ004Q3B9** – Manually test the story-line extraction (Gym demo + Main Street storylines) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: backward, choice, code, create, inspect (+20 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: choice, code, create, inspect, legacy (+18 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: code, create, critical, inspect, legacy (+17 more)

> The top match (`CG-0MLTDXG3H0WCXMUV`) is a false positive from the generic
> "choice" keyword; the curated list above is the authoritative related-work
> set.

# Migrate Gym content, fixtures and reference packs off the legacy columns

## Summary

Drop the three legacy columns from the shipped Gym storyline CSV, the story-line
fixtures, the card-pack fixtures and the Main Street reference-pack copy, then
regenerate the committed Gym manifest/Mermaid artefacts so no legacy column
survives in the content or in `node.fields`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` drops `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId` and `rejectNextCardId` from the header and every row, with every card's `options` encoding and coin/reputation deltas unchanged.
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/gym-cycle.csv`, `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack/cards.csv`, `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack/cards-duplicate.csv`, `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack-two/cards.csv` and `tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` drop the three columns, and `tests/fixtures/card-pack/helpers.ts` no longer expects `hasChoices` in the header.
- `npm run storylines:graph` regenerates `example-games/gym/content/storyline-manifest.json` and `example-games/gym/content/storyline-graph.mmd`, and neither artefact contains a legacy column key in `node.fields`.
- `npm run storylines:graph -- --check` reports no drift, and `npm run storylines:validate` passes.
- The options-parity golden snapshot from the first child still passes unchanged, proving the migration altered no compiled option list.
- Changed-scope unit tests pass and `npm run build` succeeds.
- **Satisfies parent AC3 of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI.** **Content artefacts, fixtures and schema aligned.** The Gym demo content (`example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv`) drops the three legacy columns and `GYM_CONTENT_ADAPTER` stops mapping them; the committed Gym manifest / Mermaid artefacts regenerate with no drift (`npm run storylines:graph -- --check`); card-pack fixtures, reference CSVs and `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` are updated consistently.

## Key Files

- `example-games/gym/content/storylines.csv` — header and rows drop the three legacy columns.
- `example-games/gym/content/storyline-manifest.json` — regenerated artefact.
- `example-games/gym/content/storyline-graph.mmd` — regenerated artefact.
- `tests/fixtures/story-line/gym-cycle.csv` — fixture header/rows migrated.
- `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack/cards.csv` — fixture header/rows migrated.
- `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack/cards-duplicate.csv` — fixture header/rows migrated.
- `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/fixture-game/fixture-pack-two/cards.csv` — fixture header/rows migrated.
- `tests/fixtures/card-pack/helpers.ts` — expected-header list drops `hasChoices`.
- `tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/main-street/main-street-foundations/cards.csv` — reference copy of the Main Street pack migrated.
- `tests/story-line/options-parity.test.ts` — must keep passing unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Drop the three columns from the Gym CSV and each fixture (leaving the `options` column values untouched).
2. Update the fixture header helper and any test that asserts an exact header string.
3. Regenerate the Gym artefacts and confirm `--check`, `storylines:validate` and the parity snapshot are all clean.

## Deliverables

- Legacy-free shipped content and fixtures.
- Regenerated, drift-checked Gym artefacts.
- Confirmation that compiled behaviour is unchanged (parity snapshot green).

## Dependencies

- Child "Make the content model and toolchain options-only" (the adapter must stop mapping the columns before the content drops them, so the columns never become stray `fields`).

## Provenance

Child of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI, satisfying parent AC3.

# Rename the derived manifest choice flag to `isChoice`

## Summary

The manifest's node flag is still named `hasChoices`, which collides with the
requirement that no reference to the retired legacy field survives anywhere.
It is a derived flag (computed purely from compiled options), so it is renamed
`isChoice` in the manifest type, the JSON schema, the editor view model, the
graph renderer/app shell and the committed artefacts — resolving the conflict
between parent AC2 (a derived flag may remain) and parent AC5 (no legacy field
reference may remain).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ManifestNode.hasChoices` becomes `ManifestNode.isChoice`, documented as derived from compiled options only; `renderMermaid` and every other manifest consumer use the new name.
- `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` renames the required property, and `tests/story-line/editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` validates the regenerated Gym manifest against the schema.
- The editor view model exposes `isChoice`, and `tools/storyline-editor/app-shell.ts` plus `tools/storyline-editor/graph-renderer.ts` use it (the viewer still renders choice nodes as diamonds and labels them `CHOICE · <n>`).
- The committed Gym artefacts (`storyline-manifest.json`, `storyline-graph.mmd`) are regenerated with the new property, and `npm run storylines:graph -- --check` is clean.
- A reference sweep over `src/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `example-games/` and `tests/` finds zero occurrences of `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` and `ChoiceClarityLabels`.
- Changed-scope unit and browser tests pass (editor viewer + round-trip included) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Key Files

- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — rename the node field and its derivation.
- `schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json` — rename the required/property entry.
- `src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts` — expose `isChoice`.
- `tools/storyline-editor/graph-renderer.ts` — class, `data-*` attribute and label use `isChoice`.
- `tools/storyline-editor/app-shell.ts` — details-pane kind text uses `isChoice`.
- `example-games/gym/content/storyline-manifest.json` — regenerated artefact.
- `example-games/gym/content/storyline-graph.mmd` — regenerated artefact.
- `tests/story-line/content/manifest.test.ts` — asserts the renamed field.
- `tests/story-line/editor/view-model.test.ts` — asserts the renamed field.
- `tests/story-line/editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` — schema validation of the new property.
- `tests/story-line/editor/viewer.browser.test.ts` — graph rendering of choice nodes.
- `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — manifest field reference.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Rename the manifest type field and its derivation, then the schema property.
2. Update the editor view model and the two tools modules.
3. Regenerate the artefacts, update the affected tests, and run the reference sweep.

## Deliverables

- Derived choice flag named `isChoice` end to end.
- Regenerated artefacts and a clean drift check.
- A recorded sweep result proving the four retired identifiers are gone.

## Dependencies

- Child "Migrate Gym content, fixtures and reference packs off the legacy columns" (artefact regeneration must start from legacy-free content).

## Provenance

Child of CG-0MVZBUWPH003PWUI. Producer decision (Q1-A, this planning session):
rename the derived flag rather than document it as an AC5 exception.

Renamed the derived flag end to end:
- ManifestNode.hasChoices → isChoice in src/story-line/content/manifest.ts (docstring records it is derived from compiled options only; local derivation renamed; renderMermaid uses it).
- Schema: schemas/story-line-manifest.schema.json requires/declares "isChoice" with a derived-flag description (additionalProperties:false keeps stale artefacts out).
- EditorNode.isChoice in src/story-line/editor/view-model.ts; graph-renderer.ts uses node.isChoice, the data-* attribute is now data-is-choice, and choice nodes still render as diamonds labelled CHOICE · <n>; app-shell.ts details pane uses node.isChoice.
- Committed artefacts regenerated: example-games/gym/content/storyline-manifest.json now carries "isChoice"; storyline-graph.mmd was regenerated byte-identically (Mermaid encodes choice-ness as a shape, not a field name). `npm run storylines:graph -- --check` is clean for both formats.
- docs/dev/storyline-editor.md: removed the stale optional-mapping list (it still named the retired legacy columns) and documented isChoice as derived, not mapped.

AC5 sweep (src/ tools/ scripts/ schemas/ example-games/ tests/):
  grep -rnE "hasChoices|acceptNextCardId|rejectNextCardId|ChoiceClarityLabels" src tools scripts schemas example-games tests
  → no matches (grep exit 1). The same sweep over docs/ is also empty.

Assumption recorded (AC5 vs the migration's regression guards): the only remaining references were negative assertions written by the content-migration child — they pinned the RETIRED identifiers by name (adapters.test.ts, edit-forms.test.ts, edit-roundtrip.browser.test.ts, manifest.test.ts CSV fixture header, compile.test.ts unknown-property card, ui-adapter.test.ts barrel/adapter keys, and no-legacy-columns.test.ts). Net effect: zero occurrences of the four retired identifiers anywhere, and strictly stronger guards.
